title: Slice-wise Polynomial Space Conjecture
formal: Is it true that no XNLP-hard parameterized decision problem has a single deterministic algorithm with both worst-case time \((n+2)^{f(k)}\) and working space \(f(k)(n+2)^{c}\), for any total computable function \(f:N\to N\) and any absolute constant c? Here k is the parameter, n is the bit length of the ordinary input, and both resource bounds must hold on the same execution. Hardness uses parameterized logspace many-one reductions defined below.
context:
Parameterized dynamic programs often store tables of size \(n^{O(k)}\) and run in a comparable amount of time. Allowing a larger exponent in time does not automatically show whether the memory exponent can be made independent of k.

Its machines use only a parameter-dependent multiple of log n working space while running in fixed-parameter polynomial time. Many problems on graphs with linear decompositions are complete for this class.

The target would prohibit all deterministic algorithms with a fixed polynomial space exponent while retaining polynomial time on each fixed-parameter slice. It is a simultaneous tradeoff conjecture, not a claim that the problems cannot be solved in polynomial space with unrestricted time.

The Algorithmica paper establishes XNLP-completeness for several familiar graph problems and explicitly retains this time-space assertion as Conjecture 1. Such classifications transfer the conjectured obstruction; they do not prove it.
why: Would explain a broad barrier to reducing the memory of parameterized dynamic programming while keeping polynomial time for each fixed parameter, connecting practical table-size tradeoffs with a uniform complexity-class obstruction.
status_note: Read the source’s resource/reduction definitions and the retained Algorithmica conjecture. Later-result searches through 12 September 2026, including 2026 XALP and scheduling classifications, found no resolution of the stated obstruction.

progress.text: Conjecture 14 states the simultaneous time-space obstruction and relates it to earlier work of Pilipczuk and Wrochna.
The journal study of linear graph structure retains the statement as Conjecture 1 while proving new XNLP-completeness results.

definitions: A parameterized decision problem Q is a subset of \(\{0,1\}*\times N\), with input \((x,k), n=|x|\) and k supplied in binary. XNLP consists of those Q decided by one nondeterministic multitape Turing machine using time \(g(k)(n+2)^{a}\) and working space \(g(k)\log _{2}(n+2)\) for some total computable g and constant a, simultaneously on every branch. An input is accepted exactly when some branch accepts; all branches halt within the bound. The input tape is read-only and excluded from working space, which counts visited cells on the fixed finite-alphabet work tapes. A parameterized logspace reduction \(Q_{1}\le Q_{2}\) is a deterministic halting transducer mapping \((x,k)\) to \((y,k' )\), preserving the yes/no answer, with \(k' \le h(k)\) for a total computable h and space \(h(k)+C \log _{2}(n+2)\) for an absolute C. Its output is write-only and is not counted as working space. Q is XNLP-hard when every problem in XNLP has such a reduction to Q. In the conjectured forbidden deterministic algorithm there is no randomness, oracle or advice, and a single program handles all parameters. Constants, including c and the code computing f, are fixed for that program; f may grow arbitrarily fast but must be computable. Using different computable functions in the time and space bounds is equivalent, since one common f can dominate both. Replacing n by \(n+2\) only handles short inputs. Slice-wise polynomial time allows its exponent to depend on k; the conjectured space bound permits dependence on k only in a multiplicative factor.
answer_criterion: Prove the simultaneous resource obstruction for every XNLP-hard problem, or refute it by an XNLP-hard problem and one uniform deterministic algorithm satisfying both bounds for explicit computable f and fixed c. A space bound achieved by a different algorithm, a time bound with a superpolynomial exponent in n at fixed k, or a result for only bounded parameter values does not meet the criterion.
